name: Empty Red Waterskin
summary: In Tarren Mill, an empty red waterskin is bound for a well untouched by blight. Brine gives it to shaman initiates for their elemental trials.

sections.title: A Vessel for Pure Water
sections.body: Brine gives shaman initiates this plain red skin for the Call of Water trials. They carry it across the sea to Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The Forsaken occupy the town, but its central well still draws fresh spring water. The filled skin brings a sample to Brine, who blends the water into a vial of purest water for the initiate’s trial.

faq.q: What is the Empty Red Waterskin used for?
aliases: what to do with red waterskin
faq.answer: Shaman use the skin during the Call of Water trials to gather spring water from Tarren Mill’s well. The water turns it into a Filled Red Waterskin.
Brine, an orc shaman hermit on a hill in the southern Barrens, gives the waterskin to shaman initiates undergoing elemental trials.

faq.q: Why gather water from Tarren Mill specifically?
faq.answer: Tarren Mill is under Forsaken control, yet its central well remains uncorrupted. Brine sees the pure spring as a sign of hope and life enduring in an unhallowed land.

faq.q: What happens after the waterskin is filled?
faq.answer: After filling the skin at the well, you bring it back to Brine in the Barrens. He blends its water with other rare samples into a vial of purest water, which Islen Waterseer uses to create the Water Sapta.

angles.text: As a shaman, you carry and fill this waterskin as a first step toward mastering the Water Totem and attuning your senses to water’s resilient spirits.
As an orc, you hear Brine compare the pure well in Tarren Mill to Warchief Thrall, a beacon of strength and hope enduring immense suffering.
